question.leadin: Answer some questions about the kids television series Liberty's Kids.
question.text: This American general appeared in multiple episodes of Liberty's Kids, the first of which involved disagreement between him and Ethan Allen, when they co-led the capture of Fort Ticonderoga in 1775.
question.clue: His most famous action was triggered when he was passed over for a promotion by the Continental Congress and was accused of malfeasance by other officers.

swap.text: This British Major General surrendered following the Siege of Yorktown.
swap.clue: This man's most famous act was actually performed by a proxy, General Charles O'Hara, who surrendered to Benjamin Lincoln, the subordinate of George Washington.

question.leadin: Answer the following about women in early American history.
question.text: This possibly-legendary woman took her husband's place loading cannons at the Battle of Monmouth during the American Revolution. Her nickname comes from her previous role as a water carrier.
question.answerHtml: Molly Pitcher [or Mary Ludwig Hayes McCauley; or Mary Ludwig Hayes McCauley]
question.clue: This woman fought at the Battle of Monmouth during the Revolutionary War. According to legend, her husband William collapsed during the battle, and she took his place manning artillery.

swap.leadin: Give the following about military surprise attacks launched during holidays.
swap.text: On Christmas night, 1776, George Washington's forces crossed the Delaware River and captured Hessian forces stationed in this New Jersey city.
swap.clue: There is no historical evidence that one side got drunk the night before this battle, although more than one thousand Hessians were surprised and captured by the Revolutionary Army at this battle.

question.leadin: Identify these Chief Justices of the United States.
question.text: This person held the position as a recess appointment for a few months in 1795. The Senate eventually rejected his nomination after he strongly denounced Jay's Treaty, so he retired.
question.clue: This chair of the Committee of Detail, who served as the first governor of South Carolina and second Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.

swap.text: In 1765, the passage of this act prompted representatives of nine colonies to attend a namesake conference. This act was a tax on various documents, including newspapers and playing cards.
swap.clue: A Congress named for this act held in New York passed the "Declaration of Rights and Grievances" which in part called for the end of taxation without representation.

question.leadin: In a letter written to her husband, this person asked the founding fathers to "remember the ladies."
question.text: Name this woman, the wife of the second President of the United States.
question.clue: One politician denied this woman's claims that "all men would be tyrants if they could," arguing that her requests of Congress would subject it to a "despotism of the petticoat."

swap.text: FDR's screenplay about this man was politely rejected by Paramount Pictures founder Adolph Zukor. This naval commander said, "I have not yet begun to fight!" at the Battle of Flamborough Head.
swap.clue: This naval commander raided English coastal towns during the American Revolution, and defeated the British sloop HMS Drake in 1778.

question.text: The first suspended the New York Assembly, while the second, also called the Revenue Act, laid new import taxes on glass, lead, tea, paints, and paper. They differed from the Stamp Act in requiring the customs duty to be paid at American ports. For 15 points-the Boston Tea Party and the Boston Massacre were results of what acts passed by Parliament in 1767?
question.clue: The "Massachusetts Circular" letter was written by Samuel Adams in response to this program, and these acts led to the seizure of a sloop owned by John Hancock, the Liberty.

swap.leadin: American political figures wrote numerous "Letters." Name some of those epistlers.
swap.text: This man argued that England's treatment of its colonies was legally in the wrong in his Letters from a Farmer in Pennsylvania. He also drafted the Olive Branch Petition for the Continental Congress.
swap.clue: Along with Thomas McKean, he was one of the two members of the Continental Congress to enter the military, and he opposed John Adams in the Continental Congress by voting against the Declaration of Independence.

question.text: Name the American major general in command at Bunker Hill, who later participated in the retreat from Long Island and put down a mutiny at a now-namesake camp in Redding, Connecticut during the winter of 1778 to 1779.
question.clue: He was second-in-command to Artemas Ward in the Army of Observation, and along with Ward, Philip Schuyler and Charles Lee, was one of four major generals appointed by the Continental Congress in 1775.

swap.text: One member of this family served as royal governor of New Jersey and was a key Loyalist leader during the Revolution. His father served the patriot cause as a minister to France and earlier published Poor Richard's Almanack.
swap.clue: This family, another member of which wrote articles for the New-England Courant under the pseudonym "Silence Dogood" and would go on to begin publishing the The Pennsylvania Gazette in 1728.

question.leadin: John Cadwalader shot this group's namesake in the mouth during a duel, declaring "I've stopped the damned rascal's tongue"
question.text: Name this group led by a namesake Revolutionary War officer who sought to replace George Washington with Horatio Gates.
question.clue: Another member of this group defeated Arthur St. Clair in a Pennsylvania gubernatorial election and John Cadwalader shot this group's namesake in the mouth in a duel.

swap.text: In response to the Stamp Act, Ebeneezer MacIntosh led a mob that ransacked the mansion of this Lieutenant Governor of Massachusetts due to his support of it.
swap.clue: For actually leaking this politician's letters, Benjamin Franklin was removed from his office as Postmaster General, although the public fixated on this administrator's suggestion to abridge "English liberties."

question.leadin: During this event, one party made a speech stating that no one should try to "open the floodgates of civil discord and deluge our rising empire in blood."
question.text: Identify this event in which the Continental Army threatened the newly formed United States government due to uncertainty over them receiving their pensions. George Washington managed to quell it with a good short speech.
question.clue: It followed the rejection of an impost amendment supported by its possible real organizers, Robert Morris and Alexander Hamilton.

swap.leadin: Name some people who participated in the southern theatre of the American Revolutionary War.
swap.text: This commander's surprise attack on a British camp at the Battle of Black Mingo was given away by the sound of his horses crossing a wooden bridge, but he still eluded capture by Banastre Tarleton for the duration of the war.
swap.clue: This man commanded the right flank of Nathaniel Green's army at the Battle of Eutaw Springs after leading many raids against British troops stationed between the Pee Dee and Stanee Rivers, preventing full British control of South Carolina.

question.leadin: As part of a series of boycotts on British goods, colonial women in Massachusetts were encouraged to perform this action, rather than shopping.
question.text: A 1760s movement involved what action meant to harm British business in response to the Townshend Acts?
question.answerHtml: make clothing at home [accept textiles or other synonyms in place of clothes; accept descriptive answers indicating clothes are being made rather than purchased; accept making yarn; accept Homespun movement; prompt on answers like making things at home with “what is being made?”]

swap.text: In Paris, Beaumarchais and Silas Deane encouraged this Scottish mercenary's plan to sabotage the Royal Navy dockyards in Portsmouth and Bristol by blowing them up, using flammable liquids obtained from his profession.
swap.answerHtml: John the Painter [or James Aitken or Johnny Aitken; prompt on John or James]

question.text: This employee of John Brown helped lead the raiders during the Gaspee affair. He was accused by James Wallace of burning the Gaspee.

swap.leadin: Name these financial figures from early America.
swap.text: The Bank of North America was founded in Philadelphia in 1781 by this merchant, who became superintendant of finance under the Articles of Confederation.
swap.clue: The panic of 1797 caused him to fall into debt, though the Bankruptcy Act of 1801 was written specifically to release him from prison.
